For the executive committee

One page: what it is, why now, and what we ask.

The opportunity

Judgement, not gathering

Finance teams spend most of each break, rec, variance and accrual gathering data from three to six systems before any judgement starts. That time repeats every day and every close.

What it does

Prepares, proposes, proves

Agent One Finance gathers and checks the data and proposes the outcome. Named people decide within their authority, and only approved outcomes reach the ledger.

Why it is safe

Controls in the platform

Four-eyes, delegated authority, reserved decisions, release before write-back and a full audit trail are built in once, not rebuilt per team.

The ask

A governed pilot

Sponsor a pilot with FOBO for Prime and Rates and two more Finance teams, run in shadow mode and measured against today before anyone relies on it.

The problem

Most of Finance's control work is the same job in different clothes.

A FOBO break, a cash rec difference, a P&L variance or a month-end accrual all follow the same five moves. Today each team runs them by hand, in spreadsheets and email.

A list arrives

Breaks, exceptions, alerts, complaints, journals, samples.

Data from 3–6 systems

Gathered by hand into a workbook.

Work out why

Match, recompute, compare to history.

Someone decides

Within authority, with four eyes.

Write it back

Post, repair, refund, notify, raise a ticket.

SlowHours of gathering before any thinking starts, in every team, every cycle.
Scattered evidenceFour-eyes, limits and audit trails rebuilt per team, checked differently by each auditor.
Risky with a model aloneUngrounded figures, decisions without authority, writes nobody approved.
How it works

Every capability follows the same governed path.

A team describes its work as a capability: what a case is, where the items come from, the steps, who decides and what is written back. Agent One Finance runs it the same way every time.

case
1

Get the items

Load from a system or match two. By hand, on a schedule or on an event.

2

Prepare

Rates, limits, bands, clocks, samples, timelines.

3

Propose

Rules first, then the model with read-only tools. Every figure checked.

4

People decide

Authority tiers, reserved decisions, checklists.

5

Record

Kept, learned from, re-checked on the next run.

6

Release

A second person releases; each write exactly once.

Running
Make it work

What it takes to run this for real.

The platform, the controls and the console are built. A team brings four things: its systems, its configuration, its people and a proving run.

1 · connect the systems

The ledger and the authority matrix, as connectors

Each system is an MCP connector, onboarded once. Reads and writes are marked; a write runs only after release.

journals.grnireadgoods received not invoiced, per entity and period
journals.period_status, chart_of_accountsreadis the period open; the postable accounts
authority.delegated_authorityreadthe bank's own matrix: amount bands, roles, approvals
journals.validate_journal, post_journalwritethe ledger's check first, then posting, each journal once
2 · configure the capability

About 100 lines, edited in the console

Steps, thresholds and roles. No code. Every change is checked as it is made and approved by a second owner.

steps: [load, open_period, chart, authority, accrual, material,
        group, reason, entries, draft, validate, review, record, post]
pause_before: [review, post]
policy: { materiality: 5000 GBP }
review:
  roles: [FIN_PREPARER, FIN_REVIEWER]
  authority_dataset: authority   # the bank's matrix stays the source
post: { approver_roles: [FIN_CONTROLLER] }  # never a reviewer
3 · name the people

Roles from your entitlement system

PreparersFIN_PREPARERopen the run and see everything; not above the matrix
ReviewersFIN_REVIEWERapprove within the matrix; two different reviewers over 250k
Financial controllerFIN_CONTROLLERreleases the journals to the ledger; never a reviewer of the case
Two ownerscapability ownerschange the configuration; each change approved by the other
4 · prove it, then run it

Run it locally today; shadow-run before go-live

The full build runs on a laptop with stub systems and no model. In the office, connectors point at the real systems, and an eval set checks the proposals on past periods.

# the platform, with example data
docker compose up -d postgres
cd apps/backend && .venv/bin/alembic upgrade head
.venv/bin/uvicorn agent_one_finance.web.main:app --port 8300
cd ../web && npm run dev      # http://localhost:5180

# open the September accruals run as alice
curl -X POST localhost:8300/api/capabilities/fin.accruals/cases \
  -H 'X-AOF-User: alice' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"case_key": {"entity": "UK01", "period": "2026-09"}}'

Where does our data go?

Nowhere outside the bank. Connectors read the bank's systems inside its estate, cases and audit live in the bank's PostgreSQL, and the model sees only masked fields through the bank's approved LLM endpoint.

Which model, and can we change it?

The model sits behind an adapter: the bank's approved LLM today, another tomorrow, by a setting. A capability can also run with no model at all, with rules settling what they can and people the rest.

What if the model is wrong?

Rules run first. Every figure in a proposal is checked against the data before anyone sees it. People decide, decisions above authority are refused, reserved decisions are withheld from the model, and eval sets and shadow runs prove a capability before go-live.

Can we switch it off?

Yes, per capability and for the model, instantly. Cost limits cap spend. Work falls back to people with the data still prepared.

How is it tested and audited?

Over 800 automated tests run on every change. Every data call is audited, every case has an evidence pack and a step-by-step run history, and every configuration change is approved by a second owner.

How does it scale to more teams?

By configuration: 44 building blocks, team groups for desks with their own settings, and connectors onboarded once for every capability that needs them.

Are we locked in?

No. MCP for connectors, LangGraph for orchestration, PostgreSQL for state, React for the console, and capability configuration as versioned files the bank owns.

Building blocks

44 blocks, no team-specific code.

Thresholds are named policy values, logic is expressions, and anything else is the team's own service called through the gateway. A new step type is added once and every team can use it.

    Adopt it

    From a team's process to a live capability.

    A new use case needs configuration and, at most, a connector per system. The platform team is needed only for a new connector or a new step type.

    1. Describe the work

      Guided questions, a requirements document, or a template.

    2. Connect the systems

      MCP connectors, onboarded once, read or write, scoped.

    3. Configure the steps

      Reviewers, authority, reserved decisions, tollgates, write-back.

    4. Approve the version

      A second owner approves; until then nothing runs on it.

    5. Prove it

      Eval sets and shadow runs against past cases.

    6. Run it

      By hand, on a schedule or on another system's event.

    7. Improve it

      Recurring items, the unexplained, judgement calls ready to become rules.

    8. Add team groups

      Other desks run it with their own settings, within what it allows.

    Rollout

    Prove it on FOBO, then scale across Finance.

    Each stage passes a gate before the next begins. No stage relies on the model until its proposals have been measured against today's work.

    1. 1 · Shadow pilot

      FOBO for Prime and Rates runs beside today's process on the same books and dates.

      Gate: eval set passes; controllers agree the proposals

    2. 2 · Go live

      Controllers work FOBO cases in the console; the platform measures time per decision.

      Gate: Product Control signs off; model use approved

    3. 3 · Two more teams

      Month-end accruals and reconciliations on the same platform, by configuration.

      Gate: connectors onboarded; owners named

    4. 4 · Across Finance

      Teams onboard their own capabilities; the platform team adds connectors and new step types.

      Gate: measured hours and audit outcomes reviewed
    Fit

    Where Agent One Finance fits, and where it does not.

    A strong fit

    • Work that arrives as a list of items, each needing an investigation and an accountable decision.
    • Data spread over several systems that someone gathers by hand today.
    • Controls that matter: four-eyes, authority limits, evidence for audit.
    • Repeating work, daily, monthly or per event, where yesterday's decisions inform today's.

    Not what it is for

    • Not a system of record. Ledgers, payment engines and KYC systems keep their data and controls.
    • Not an autonomous decision-maker. It never clears a screening hit or releases a payment.
    • Not real-time. Cases take seconds to minutes; in-flight checks belong in the transaction path.
    • Not forms and routing alone. Work with no investigation is better served elsewhere.
    Next step

    Bring one process. Leave with a running capability.

    Pick a use case with a named owner and its systems in reach. The platform, the controls and the console are already there; what remains is the team's own configuration.

    • From leadership: an executive sponsor, and the FOBO pilot with Prime and Rates as the first stage.
    • From technology: the connectors to the ledger and MB Rec, and the bank's LLM endpoint for the pilot.
    • From risk: model use approved under the model risk policy, and the reserved decisions agreed.
    1. The process: the list of items, and what a decision on one looks like.
    2. The owners: who decides, who releases, and the authority limits.
    3. The systems: what is read, and what the outcome is written to.
    4. The boundaries: what risk and compliance reserve for named people.
